_comment: Single source of truth for all superseded and retracted performance figures, strawman numbers, and refuted mechanism claims.
Asserted across all tracked markdown, HTML visualizer, JSON datasets, and benchmark docs by scripts/check_docs_hygiene.py and crates/expanse/tests/test_visualizer_sync.rs.

figures.rationale: Pre-repair random 1M lookup deficit measured under load; quiet host measures 1.031x

figures.replacement: Retracted as unmeasured rescaled instruction counts (~5.52 instr/ns)
figures.rationale: Wall-clock ns figures were rescaled instruction counts, never actually measured

figures.replacement: Bounded keyspace measurement (0.12x-0.55x negative scaling on 50/50 mix, 11.4x on read-only)
figures.rationale: Probed unbounded random u64 keys measuring near-100%-miss descent walk

figures.replacement: Workload E re-measured with symmetric predicate (BTreeMap wins Workload E)
figures.rationale: Asymmetric scan predicate passed ~100% vs ~50% for baselines; 13.2 B/entry for RocksDB is valid and exempt
Strawman static 16-pointer tower baseline vs fair variable-height skiplist

figures.replacement: Unmeasured mechanism tracked in #480 (hardware counter shows 0.042 LLC misses vs 2.74 branch mispredicts)
figures.rationale: LLC miss count is near zero, refuting memory latency bottleneck

figures.replacement: indistinguishable at the recorded resolution: intersection() < 100 ns, intersection_len() < 10 ns (docs/benchmarks/set_algebra/results/bench_domain_algebra.json)
figures.rationale: Both arms recorded to 0.1 us / 0.01 us; equal values at a finite resolution bound the difference below it and cannot establish zero. The claim asserted a precision 100x finer than the source carries (§8.4).

figures.replacement: host and commit unresolved per section; see docs/benchmarks/set_algebra/README.md
figures.rationale: One host field and one commit covered five sections across two harnesses; no section's host is recoverable, and the cells appear in no committed artifact. Withdrawn rather than reassigned (§8.10).

figures.replacement: 1.007x-1.031x measured over 4 clean repetitions on the reference host; 11.69 M keys/s text, 5.75 M keys/s UUID (docs/benchmarks/set_algebra/README.md)
figures.rationale: Measured 1.007x-1.031x across 8 cells; published throughput is ~2.5x lower and the published speedup ~3x higher than measurement, so the published pair cannot have come from this harness.

figures.replacement: 604.4 M keys/s (1.655 ns/key) at N=10k, 609.5 M keys/s (1.641 ns/key) at N=100k (docs/benchmarks/set_algebra/README.md)
figures.rationale: Measured ~37x faster. The published pair matches the criterion TOTAL scan time at N=10k (16.55 us) read as a per-key throughput, with 61 ns derived from it as 1/16.4M.

figures.replacement: 1.0013 [1.0009, 1.0015] (+0.1%), 288.9 ns raw / 289.2 ns domain at commit fcca1c0d (docs/benchmarks/set_algebra/results/bench_domain_algebra.json)
figures.rationale: Measured at c4b1817f before #638 changed the cardinality walk (runtime popcnt dispatch) and before #701 pinned the harness allocator policy; re-measured over 5 independent runs the resolved ~5% overhead reads 0.1%. Superseded, not silently overwritten (§8.7).

figures.replacement: 7.17× (377.4 vs 52.7 cycles per key walked) at bec51c48 after #694; the paired capture across #694 moved the arm 461.45 -> 371.10 (docs/benchmarks/embedded/results/esp32.json, results/pairing_694/)
figures.rationale: The 49b3b6c1 device artifact predated #694 (running rank through the C ABI range walk); a paired capture across that change moved the aggregate arm by a fifth, four times the layout floor, and the headline was re-harvested at bec51c48. Superseded, not silently overwritten (§8.7).

figures.replacement: M4 ingest 7.3x (2,967 vs 406) and 3.1x (2,967 vs 971), M4 CAN dispatch 1,211 (6,045 ns), M7 400 MHz cache-on bulk remove_range 856 / 2,136 ns at fce563c2; paired capture 22908c15 -> fce563c2 in docs/benchmarks/stm32h747/results/pairing_fce563c2/
figures.rationale: The 22908c15 STM32 artifact predated #667/#698 (constant-length read_rem and set_immed_keys), which the paired capture moved the eviction fixtures 6-24% on both cores; the whole artifact was re-harvested at fce563c2 and these were its most-quoted cells. Superseded, not silently overwritten (§8.7).

patterns: fails safe rather than silently wrong
figures.replacement: M4 ingest 7.4x (2,964 vs 403) and 3.0x (2,964 vs 988), M4 CAN dispatch 1,237 (6,177 ns) at a98d8d3c under the DWT-profile harness; the cacheable-heap cross-core cell returned wrong values in two of eight captures and does not fail safe (docs/benchmarks/stm32h747/README.md, results/pairing_dwt_a98d8d3c/)
figures.rationale: The fce563c2 artifact was taken with the harness before the DWT-profile rows; the same engine re-harvested under the new harness moved the M7 cells up to 4.8% by code placement alone, so its cells are superseded by the a98d8d3c artifact. The 'fails safe' reading of the unsupported cacheable configuration rested on captures that landed in the all-BUSY mode; two later captures returned corrupted values. Superseded, not silently overwritten (§8.7).
